_why: Where every screenshot of the SHOWCASE comes from, so a screen that moved can be retaken instead of guessed at: a demo instance with a rich dataset and live traffic, chosen to show the product. The loop is in scripts/screenshots.mjs, and the pictures are img/showcase/*, used by the showcase page alone. The documentation's screenshots are another job - each shows the state its page explains - and are retaken by e2e/scripts/capture-docs.mjs into img/console/*. Neither writes the other's files.

instance.console: the binary must EMBED the console, or the admin port answers a JSON status page: make ui first, or stage console/dist/console/browser into internal/admin/ui/dist
instance.edition: Enterprise (-tags ee): the console's EE badges and the Enterprise screens are part of what is shown
instance.upstream: node scripts/screenshots-upstream.mjs  (keeps running on 127.0.0.1:8099): the instance reaches the routes' services - http://docs:8080 and http://orders-api:8080, names of a stack - through it, as HTTP_PROXY; Billing is left out of the proxy on purpose (NO_PROXY), so the routes list shows a target that is down
instance.run: HOSTNAME=meerkat-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p MEERKAT_VERSION=1.0.1 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8099 NO_PROXY=billing.svc.acme.internal MEERKAT_TENANCY=multi MEERKAT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=test1234 /tmp/meerkat-doc -addr :8086 -admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9096 -internal-addr 127.0.0.1:7096 -data /tmp/docdata
instance.seed: node scripts/screenshots-seed.mjs  (once, on an EMPTY data directory)
instance.ports: 8086/9096 and 8087/9097 on purpose: this repository's own dev instance runs on 8082 and 9092 and must never be disturbed
instance.dataset: Acme Corp (the primary organisation, renamed), its logo and tagline. Five routes, their services named as in a stack: Billing, Docs portal, Orders API, Inventory (maintenance), Catch-all. A role tree of nine roles with tags under three top-level roles, five accounts besides admin (one app admin, one infra admin), three groups (Finance, Front desk, Warehouse), a vault with two secrets and a value that routes use, a portal bar, two self-signed certificates and three TLS names, three control-plane tokens and two application tokens, two saved configurations, three schedules (a cadence, a cron line, one date), an OpenTelemetry collector at http://opentelemetry:4318, and the few updates the Audit caption describes. Orders API carries a deposited OpenAPI spec of 14 operations, five endpoint rules (a closed operation with a named exception, two role rules, two rate limits) and two audited operations. All in scripts/screenshots-seed.mjs.
instance.traffic: the Metrics screen shows the last minute only: screenshots.mjs starts `screenshots-seed.mjs --traffic-only` itself for the shots marked traffic, and takes them last
instance.host: gateway.acme.example: the name the browser is shown, mapped to 127.0.0.1 by Chromium (--host-resolver-rules), so no capture says localhost. The data plane listens on :8086 without an address, so the console derives the applications' origin from that name

loopback.why: what the seed and the traffic use: Node resolves no made-up name

instance.version: MEERKAT_VERSION=1.0.1: the binary is built as dev, and the account menu and the release notes then read as a release, not as a development build

single.why: Application, Groups and Members exist only when the installation serves one organisation (singleTenantOnly); in multi mode the same tables live under each tenant, with the tenant's own navigation
single.run: HOSTNAME=meerkat-7d9f8c6b5-x2k4p MEERKAT_VERSION=1.0.1 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8099 NO_PROXY=billing.svc.acme.internal MEERKAT_TENANCY=single MEERKAT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=test1234 /tmp/meerkat-doc -addr :8087 -admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9097 -internal-addr 127.0.0.1:7097 -data /tmp/docdata-single
